author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Roger Williams Park Zoo is mourning Zipper, a 27-year-old zebra that was euthanized after suffering a critical wound believed to have been caused by another animal in her habitat.

The zoo’s animal-care, veterinary and operations teams arranged for a large-animal surgical and anesthesia team from Tufts University to assist with emergency treatment. After evaluating the injury, the teams determined it was not survivable, according to a report by NBC 10 WJAR.
Staff remembered Zipper as a confident, familiar presence with a strong interest in carrots. She had spent 27 years at the Providence zoo and was well known to employees and visitors.

The loss also creates an immediate animal-care concern for Tundra, the zoo’s remaining zebra. Staff said Tundra was closely attached to Zipper and often waited for her before going inside or eating. Because zebras are herd animals, the zoo is monitoring Tundra and working to bring in new companions. The care team is also reviewing what happened and considering changes intended to reduce the risk of a similar injury. No further details about the other animal or the precise circumstances of the wound were released in the initial account.
dek: Veterinary teams determined the 27-year-old zebra’s wound was not survivable; the zoo is monitoring her longtime companion and reviewing the incident.
headline: Roger Williams Park Zoo mourns Zipper the zebra after critical injury
